faqs.q: Who supplies hydraulic hose and fittings to Kampala from Dubai?
faqs.a: Indus Hydraulics ships hydraulic hose, fittings, adapters, valves, industrial hose and oilfield equipment from Dubai to Uganda. Containers sail from Jebel Ali to Mombasa and move by road on the Northern Corridor through Malaba to Kampala in typically 20–26 days, and urgent parts fly into Entebbe in three to five days. We arrange the UNBS Certificate of Conformity before the vessel sails, so the consignment is ready to clear.

faqs.q: Why does a shipment to Kampala take longer than one to Nairobi?
faqs.a: Because the lane has two halves. The container discharges at Mombasa and then travels by road through Malaba, clearing once as Kenyan transit and again as a Ugandan import. The sea leg is the predictable part; the road leg is where most of the variability and cost sits, so every quotation names exactly where our responsibility ends.

faqs.q: What is the UNBS PVoC certificate and who arranges it?
faqs.a: Regulated goods entering Uganda need a UNBS Certificate of Conformity under the PVoC programme, issued per consignment before the vessel sails. We arrange it through an appointed PVoC agent from the part numbers on the order. Because the certificate is issued in Dubai before loading, the part list has to be complete at quotation rather than at order.

faqs.q: Which documents travel with a consignment to Uganda?
faqs.a: The UNBS Certificate of Conformity, issued before sailing; Kenyan transit documents for the corridor leg, handled by the nominated forwarder at Mombasa; a Certificate of Origin attested by the Dubai Chamber; and the bill of lading with our packing list. Material and test certificates from the mill or our test bench are added where the order calls for them.

faqs.q: Can you route Uganda cargo through Dar es Salaam instead of Mombasa?
faqs.a: Yes, on the Central Corridor. Sea to Dar es Salaam and road onward runs typically 24–30 days against 20–26 via Mombasa, so it is the alternative when Mombasa is congested rather than the default. We quote both routes when the order is large enough for the difference to matter.

faqs.q: Can you supply the Albertine oil projects at Tilenga and Kingfisher?
faqs.a: Yes. Wellhead, BOP, flow iron and drilling hose are core catalogue, rated to API 6A, API 16A and API 7K, with NACE MR0175 documentation where the contract requires it. We supply TechnipFMC, Cameron (SLB), SPM, Anson, Stream-Flo and WOM equipment, and quote DAP to site for contractors working around Hoima and Buliisa.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to Hoima, Buliisa and other sites west of Kampala?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms to the site gate. The leg west of Kampala to Hoima, Buliisa, Fort Portal or Kasese is quoted rather than estimated, because site access and the road leg vary by job. Buyers who already clear their own goods can instead take delivery CIF Mombasa and let their agent run the corridor.

faqs.q: Is air freight into Entebbe worth it for urgent parts?
faqs.a: For a machine that is down, usually yes. Air freight from Dubai to Entebbe takes three to five days from dispatch and is quoted per shipment. It skips both the sea leg and the corridor, which makes it the right answer for a plant-down and an expensive one for a planned order; planned work normally moves by sea and road via Mombasa.

faqs.q: Can you make up hydraulic hose assemblies to length for Ugandan plant fleets?
faqs.a: Yes. Assemblies are crimped and pressure-tested in Dubai and shipped as finished items, each tagged with the hose, the fittings and the test date. Send the hose standard — SAE J517, EN 853, EN 856 or ISO 18752 — with the end fittings and cut length, and the assembly arrives ready to fit on excavators, cranes and drilling plant.

faqs.q: Do you supply spares for the hydropower stations on the Nile?
faqs.a: Yes. Gate operator cylinders, governor hydraulics, high-pressure hose and fittings are standard supply for hydropower plant, with material and test certificates where the order calls for them. For stations such as Bujagali, Isimba and Karuma we quote DAP to site or CIF Mombasa, and suggest listing mating seals and fittings with the main item given the length of the lane.

faqs.q: How do I get a quotation for delivery to Kampala?
faqs.a: Send the part numbers or specifications, quantities and the delivery point — Mombasa, Kampala or your site. We quote in AED or USD on the Incoterm you choose: DAP Kampala or site, CIF Mombasa, FOB Jebel Ali, or EXW Dubai for a nominated forwarder. faqs.q: Who supplies hydraulic hose and fittings to Eritrea from Dubai?
faqs.a: Indus Hydraulics ships hydraulic hose, fittings, adapters, valves and industrial hose from Dubai to Eritrea. Containers sail from Jebel Ali to Massawa in typically 10–14 days, or to Assab in 12–16 days for southern deliveries, and air freight reaches Asmara in three to five days. faqs.q: Why is the paperwork slower than the freight to Eritrea?
faqs.a: Because the import licence and the foreign exchange approval both come before shipment, not after it. The consignee obtains the licence with the ministry and the exchange approval through its bank. The sea leg to Massawa is only ten to fourteen days, so in practice the permissions, rather than the voyage or the picking in Dubai, decide when goods arrive.

faqs.q: What do you need from an Eritrean buyer to start an order?
faqs.a: The part list and the consignee’s registered details. With those we issue a quotation in a form the import licence application and the foreign exchange approval can be made against. The invoice and packing list are issued in the consignee’s registered name, so it helps to send the details exactly as registered. We then hold the order until both permissions are granted.

faqs.q: Which documents are needed to import hydraulic equipment into Eritrea?
faqs.a: An import licence, obtained by the consignee with the ministry, and a foreign exchange approval from the consignee’s bank, both before shipment. We then supply a Certificate of Origin attested by the Dubai Chamber and the invoice and packing list in the consignee’s registered name, with material and test certificates from the mill or our test bench where the order calls for them.

faqs.q: Should cargo go to Massawa or Assab?
faqs.a: Massawa for Asmara, Keren and the north: typically 10–14 days from Jebel Ali. Assab for deliveries in the Southern Red Sea region, at 12–16 days, because it saves a long inland leg. If your site sits between the two, tell us the delivery point at quotation and we price the route that keeps the inland distance shortest.

faqs.q: Can you supply Eritrea’s copper, zinc, gold and potash mines?

faqs.q: Is air freight into Asmara available?

Planned orders normally travel by sea to Massawa.

faqs.q: Why is the Eritrea lane quoted per consignment rather than on a schedule?

faqs.q: Can you provide the certificates a project specification calls for?
faqs.a: Yes, on request, and it is best agreed at the enquiry. When an item is bought against a written specification, what has to arrive is the part and the evidence: a certificate of conformity, the standard it was built to, and a document trail that survives an audit. faqs.q: Can you supply the gold operations in eastern Senegal?

The inland leg from Dakar through Tambacounda is long, so it is quoted rather than estimated, and the delivery point is named on the document set from the start. faqs.q: Can you route cargo on to Mali through Dakar?

faqs.q: How do I request a quotation from Senegal?

We quote in USD on CIF Dakar, DAP to site, FOB Jebel Ali or EXW Dubai for your forwarder, and agree the French descriptions and tariff lines at the same time.
